The assessment typically spans several months and follows an iterative process where findings are remediated by ServiceNow security and development teams. Results of these penetration tests are available to customers and prospects under NDA via the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal.

## Best practices

### Create a process to examine ServiceNow penetration test reports periodically
Create a process to ensure stakeholders, such as your security team, review the most recent published [ServiceNow penetration test reports](#) on the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#).

## Activate the ServiceNow Access Control (SNAC) plugin for enhanced control
Customers may choose to activate the [ServiceNow access control plugin](#), which enables customers to control which ServiceNow customer service and support employees can access their instance, and when. Review the plugin with stakeholders to determine if it needs to be enabled. Once this control is enabled, ServiceNow personnel must request ad-hoc, time-bound access.

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow, as the data processor, supports customer incident response by querying backend logs upon request, subject to an eight-week retention limit. While customers are responsible for interpreting logs, [ServiceNow Support](#) can help review samples to clarify log types. However, it is essential to note that ServiceNow Support does not have the resources to analyze every event.

ServiceNow Support and security teams assist in identifying possible causes of incidents and offer preventive guidance, though recommendations may be limited by platform capabilities.

At an enterprise level, security teams at ServiceNow have implemented detection rules that initiate internal incident response processes. Detections related to customer instances are normally reported through a support case.

### Best practices

#### Address noncompliance with security hardening and hardening compliance score
Use [Security hardening](https://www.servicenow.com) to identify, test, and assess noncompliance in a sub-production instance. Review the hardening compliance score to determine how closely your instance aligns with SSC hardening recommendations.

*Note: A high compliance score does not guarantee that the instance is fully secure—it only reflects alignment with SSC hardening settings.*

#### Run Security Center security scans regularly
The [Security scanner](https://www.servicenow.com) helps discover and correct access control misconfigurations. Use the Security Scanner built-in to SSC to scan your instance against a set of security checks in order to identify misconfigurations on a regular cadence.

## Best practices

### Choose an encryption method for data at rest in an instance*
The customer’s security team should work with stakeholders to thoroughly assess the regulatory and organizational requirements for data stored in their ServiceNow instance(s) to determine if data at rest needs to be encrypted.

Based on this assessment, customers should select the most appropriate encryption method offered by ServiceNow. When implementing the chosen encryption method, ensure encryption settings and key management are configured in accordance with internal policies and compliance standards to safeguard sensitive information throughout its lifecycle.

### Customers seeking included functionality
**Field Encryption Starter**:  
Data stored within a ServiceNow instance can be protected with Field Encryption Starter, which allows customers to encrypt specific fields within the instance using AES128 or AES256 encryption.

# Best practices

## Understand the ServiceNow Data Sharing Program
Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to fully understand how anonymized data is shared with ServiceNow. Confirm the intended data contribution strategy with appropriate stakeholders. Customers of the Advanced AI and Data Products can opt out of sharing data.

Refer to the [Data Sharing Programs](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=b16448406) and [AI Model Improvement](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=b16448406) for details on how ServiceNow collects and uses customer-contributed data to enhance AI models, as per the [product-specific terms](https://www.servicenow.com/store).

- Customers can opt out of anonymized data sharing within 30 days of downloading an AI app from the [ServiceNow Store](https://www.servicenow.com/store).
- Data sharing for the Advanced AI and Data Products can be managed from the Now Assist Admin Console.

### Consider additional restriction policies
Customers can implement [cross-origin resource sharing (CORS)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS) rules to control which domains can access specific REST API endpoints. Adaptive Authentication policies can be applied specifically to APIs, restricting both the API endpoint and the web methods employed. ACLs can be required for scripted APIs. An API access policy sets permissions and access duration, allowing you to control inbound ServiceNow API access according to authentication type and filter criteria. The following are the three levels of auth policy support for non-interactive sessions:

### Consider your AI security strategy:
- **Engage key stakeholders**: Identify all stakeholders involved throughout the AI lifecycle and clearly define and document their roles and responsibilities.
- **Define system purpose**: Clearly articulate the task and intended purpose of each AI system.
- **Enable human oversight**: Establish procedures that allow authorized personnel to interrupt, override, or halt system operations when necessary.
- **Provide contestability**: Implement mechanisms for challenging automated decisions, ensuring human operators can review actions taken by AI systems and, if appropriate, supplement them.

Customers should establish accountability for AI-driven processes and implement appropriate controls to guard against unintended outcomes.

# Key concepts and reference material

## Intended audience
This guide is specifically designed for instance administrators to collaborate closely with security and compliance professionals. Engaging both parties is essential to effectively address the evolving landscape of digital threats, demonstrate due diligence, and sustain a robust security posture across the ServiceNow environment.

## Identify stakeholders
At the outset of a best practice review, instance administrators are advised to identify the primary security and compliance stakeholders within their organization. Their expertise and insights will help tailor the best practices to the organization’s specific risk profile and compliance requirements.

Engaging these partners early in the process not only streamlines decision making but also strengthens the organization’s overall security posture throughout the ServiceNow environment.

### Harden the MID Server and operating system
Deploy and secure the MID Server’s operating system and runtime environment according to your organization’s IT security policies. Use only [supported operating systems](#) that receive security updates. The MID Server Java application runs on supported Windows or Linux servers with a Java Runtime Environment.

### Harden server and operating system for MID Server security
Ensure that the server operating system and runtime environment are deployed, secured, and hardened in accordance with the organization’s established internal IT security policies and operational procedures. Operate only on supported operating systems that continue to receive security updates. The MID Server Java application runs on supported Windows or Linux Servers with a Java Runtime Environment.

# RESPOND

## Incident management

### Customer responsibility
During an incident, customers must lead investigations based on their internal processes, security needs, and regulatory obligations, as ServiceNow cannot anticipate these specifics. In addition, ServiceNow asks that customers keep their security contacts updated in the event that ServiceNow needs to reach out for a suspected incident.

While ServiceNow can assist with questions on the investigation, customers are responsible for classifying related behavior as malicious or benign, given their contextual knowledge. [ServiceNow Support](#) can help interpret log samples but cannot review all logs or determine the full scope of an incident.

To ensure effective assistance, customers are responsible for providing detailed information—such as timelines, IPs, and user data—when requesting support. Broad log queries can delay investigations, whereas targeted data enables faster resolution.

```markdown
# DETECT

## Logging and monitoring

### Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for managing and monitoring security-related information within their ServiceNow instance. Extensive logging of transactions, events, and system-level activity is stored in tables within the customer’s instance. Customers have access to:
- End-user activity  
- Failed login attempts  
- Audit trails and record histories  
- Administrative escalations  
- Access by ServiceNow support personnel  

ServiceNow AI Platform transaction logs are retained within the instance for approximately 30 days, event logs for about 7 days, and audit records are retained indefinitely within the instance.

---

## Best practices

### Choose an encryption method for data at rest in an instance*
The customer’s security team should work with stakeholders to thoroughly assess the regulatory and organizational requirements for data stored in their ServiceNow instance(s) to determine if data at rest needs to be encrypted.

Based on this assessment, customers should select the most appropriate encryption method offered by ServiceNow. When implementing the chosen encryption method, ensure encryption settings and key management are configured in accordance with internal policies and compliance standards to safeguard sensitive information throughout its lifecycle.

### Customers seeking included functionality
**Field Encryption Starter**:  
Data stored within a ServiceNow instance can be protected with Field Encryption Starter, which allows customers to encrypt specific fields within the instance using AES128 or AES256 encryption.

*Note:* Negotiated ciphers are subject to customer browser versions and may be influenced by customer Internet proxy infrastructure. Customers can specify cipher suites in their own browsers or proxies, as well as select the ciphers to be used on their instance.

#### Configure other protocols for encryption in transit
Admins can also configure other traffic protocols, such as LDAP, SMTP, and SFTP, to use TLS 1.2.

#### Encrypt email via S/MIME
ServiceNow implementations can support [S/MIME “end-to-end” email encryption](https://www.servicenow.com).
```

# DETECT

## Logging and monitoring

### Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for managing and monitoring security-related information within their ServiceNow instance. Extensive logging of transactions, events, and system-level activity is stored in tables within the customer’s instance. Customers have access to:
- End-user activity  
- Failed login attempts  
- Audit trails and record histories  
- Administrative escalations  
- Access by ServiceNow support personnel  

ServiceNow AI Platform transaction logs are retained within the instance for approximately 30 days, event logs for about 7 days, and audit records are retained indefinitely within the instance.</DOCUMENT>

## Best practices

### Choose an encryption method for data at rest in an instance*
The customer’s security team should work with stakeholders to thoroughly assess the regulatory and organizational requirements for data stored in their ServiceNow instance(s) to determine if data at rest needs to be encrypted.

Based on this assessment, customers should select the most appropriate encryption method offered by ServiceNow. When implementing the chosen encryption method, ensure encryption settings and key management are configured in accordance with internal policies and compliance standards to safeguard sensitive information throughout its lifecycle.

### Customers seeking included functionality
**Field Encryption Starter**:

Admins can also configure other traffic protocols, such as LDAP, SMTP, and SFTP, to use TLS 1.2.

#### Address noncompliance with security hardening and hardening compliance score
Use [Security hardening](https://www.servicenow.com) to identify, test, and assess noncompliance in a sub-production instance. Review the hardening compliance score to determine how closely your instance aligns with SSC hardening recommendations.

*Note: A high compliance score does not guarantee that the instance is fully secure—it only reflects alignment with SSC hardening settings.*

#### Run Security Center security scans regularly
The [Security scanner](https://www.servicenow.com) helps discover and correct access control misconfigurations. Use the Security Scanner built-in to SSC to scan your instance against a set of security checks in order to identify misconfigurations on a regular cadence.

## Understand how to review logs for investigations
One of the most important components of incident response is ServiceNow instance logs. These [system logs](https://support.servicenow.com), will be able to provide customers’ security teams with the necessary telemetry for their incident response investigations. Logs can be reviewed using a variety of methods, such as the [log file browser](https://support.servicenow.com), Table APIs, and directly in the platform.

## Conduct postmortem activities following a security incident
Following a security incident, it is important to perform a postmortem review of the investigations to determine possible improvements that can be made for future incident response activities. This can include identifying possible communication issues, gaps within the environment’s security posture, and ensuring all involved parties understand the root cause of the issue and how to avoid similar situations moving forward.

---

#### Ensure security communications from ServiceNow are properly routed
Ensure that your ServiceNow security contacts are updated and security-related COMM records are not being filtered to spam folders. Security contacts can be updated on [ServiceNow Support](#) by a member of the customer’s platform team and should receive an email notification for security-related notifications when they are sent. These notifications can come from sources such as cases created for a ServiceNow-detected security incident and COMM records.

---

This guide is specifically designed for instance administrators to collaborate closely with security and compliance professionals. # Physical security and environmental controls

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow performs colocation facility vendor reviews annually and periodically performs onsite assessments of physical and environmental controls.

ServiceNow colocation facility operations, security, and procurement personnel review the colocation facility provider SOC 2 Type 2 reports or other available assessments (e.g., ISO 27001) on an annual basis.

Additionally, through periodic visits to the facility, ServiceNow colocation facility operations and compliance personnel review the controls applicable to the services provided to ServiceNow.

- Routine meetings are held with vendor account management personnel to help ensure services are provided according to expectations.
- Cloud operations personnel review access activity within the colocation facility suites on a periodic basis to ensure access is appropriate.

### Best practices
**Review and understand physical security and environmental controls at ServiceNow**

In this document, security and compliance is considered from the perspective of the [National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF)](https://). The CSF is a set of voluntary guidelines, standards, and practices made available by NIST, an agency of the United States Department of Commerce.

This Best Practices Guide is also available in the following languages: [Spanish](https://), [French](https://), [German](https://), [Dutch](https://), [Italian](https://), [Brazilian Portuguese](https://), [Korean](https://), and [Japanese](https://).

Note: All information in this white paper is related to the standard ServiceNow Commercial Cloud.

### Best practices

#### Understand your organization’s incident response escalation channels
One of the most important variables during a security incident is the time between the incident being reported and when your security team is alerted. To minimize this time as much as possible, ensure that you understand the appropriate contacts within your organization that need to be alerted when an incident is reported. This could be an email address, a catalog item within your internal resources, or a post to a messaging channel. - **Storage**: BYOK’s should be stored in a secure, protected environment that performs regular backups to ensure that the keys remain available and recoverable, if needed.

Some ServiceNow products rely on third-party Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) services, such as Azure OpenAI. # MID Server security

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for ensuring the security of the MID Server by maintaining strict physical controls, deploying and hardening the server and operating system in accordance with their internal IT policies, and restricting network access to only essential services and infrastructure. They are also responsible for operating the MID Server and managing account credentials. Additionally, customers must monitor firewall and proxy configurations to allow only the necessary connections.

---

## Best practices

### Secure physical access to the MID Server
Place the MID Server in a physically secure location, such as a locked data center or server room, with access restricted to authorized personnel. Follow your organization’s access audit requirements to detect and prevent unauthorized entry.

As the data controller, the customer is responsible for determining how data is collected, stored, used, shared, archived, destroyed, and for maintaining the accuracy and confidentiality of that data. The customer is also responsible for meeting their requirements as a data controller under the applicable data protection laws.

Additionally, customers are responsible for risks associated with their AI investments. ServiceNow has a premium offering, called AI Control Tower, that can give customers visibility into their AI footprint by managing their AI asset inventory, configuration, state of AI cases, and approval flows.

---

Deploy and secure the MID Server’s operating system and runtime environment according to your organization’s IT security policies. ### Harden server and operating system for MID Server security
Ensure that the server operating system and runtime environment are deployed, secured, and hardened in accordance with the organization’s established internal IT security policies and operational procedures. Operate only on supported operating systems that continue to receive security updates. The MID Server Java application runs on supported Windows or Linux Servers with a Java Runtime Environment.

---

## Best practices

### Secure physical access to the MID Server
Place the MID Server in a physically secure location, such as a locked data center or server room, with access restricted to authorized personnel. Follow your organization’s access audit requirements to detect and prevent unauthorized entry.

### Key ownership and control
Customers need to determine which type of encryption key they will use on the ServiceNow AI Platform: a ServiceNow-managed key (SMK) or bring your own key (BYOK).

### Encryption key lifecycle management
- **Generation**: When using BYOK, keys should be generated in accordance with the company’s internal security policy and follow the [ServiceNow key preparation guidance](https://example.com).

- **Storage**: BYOK’s should be stored in a secure, protected environment that performs regular backups to ensure that the keys remain available and recoverable, if needed.

---

## Best practices

## Data processing in production
When using generative AI services, prompts and responses are processed in memory only—inputs and outputs are not stored or cached by the inference infrastructure. For details on how data is transmitted, processed, and protected during runtime, refer to the [Data Processing for Advanced AI & Data Products FAQ (KB1584492)](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=kb1584492).

Evaluate how AI data is securely processed and select either ServiceNow-hosted or third-party LLMs in alignment with your organization’s data residency and governance policies.

*Note:* Third-party LLMs may use global infrastructure to dynamically route traffic to the best available data center for each request. This means the regional processing location may differ from the data center region specified on a customer’s order form.

- **Full direct-to-disk backups** are performed every seven days and retained for a minimum of 14 days
- **Differential backups** are taken every 24 hours

Sub-production instances (commonly used for testing and development purposes) are backed up only in their primary colocation facility, because they are not AHA-capable.

Through the Patching Program, ServiceNow delivers regular updates that include security, performance, and functional fixes to customer instances. ServiceNow enforces an End-of-Life (EOL) policy to ensure that only supported versions receive updates, helping maintain a secure and stable platform for all customers.

### Best practices  

#### Regularly review the ServiceNow security advisories page  
These advisories often highlight vulnerabilities addressed through patches or upgrades, ensuring customers can apply updates promptly to maintain security and compliance. Work with stakeholders, such as the security team, when necessary to apply, mitigate and patch the ServiceNow instance, as needed.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>- **The colocation facility** and the third-party **cloud service provider** (CSP) also have shared responsibilities with the data controller (customer) and data processor (ServiceNow).

For more information about security responsibilities concerning customer data, see the [ServiceNow Shared Responsibility Model overview](#).

This document includes shared responsibilities specified at the beginning of each section. Customers should review each customer responsibility with relevant stakeholders to ensure the organization fully understands its obligations as specified in the ServiceNow Shared Responsibility Model. Relevant stakeholders may include architecture teams, security teams, and compliance personnel.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>```markdown
# Best practices continued

## Know the difference between software updates and upgrades
Understanding the difference between a software update and an upgrade is essential for maintaining both security and support in your ServiceNow environment.

- **Software updates:** Patches and platform fixes delivered throughout the year via the ServiceNow Patching Program. These address known vulnerabilities and improve performance without changing the platform version.
- **Upgrades:** Moving to a newer major platform version, typically released twice a year, which includes enhanced features, architectural improvements, and broader functionality.

Both are critical but serve different purposes in keeping your instance secure, stable, and supported.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>#### Ensure security communications from ServiceNow are properly routed
Ensure that your ServiceNow security contacts are updated and security-related COMM records are not being filtered to spam folders. Security contacts can be updated on [ServiceNow Support](#) by a member of the customer’s platform team and should receive an email notification for security-related notifications when they are sent. These notifications can come from sources such as cases created for a ServiceNow-detected security incident and COMM records.

---

November 2025 | Release: Zurich
```</DOCUMENT>

### Best practices

#### Ensure key stakeholders have access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal
Establish a formal procedure to identify relevant parties, including compliance teams, vendor risk assessment teams, and security personnel who require access to CORE documentation for internal audits and vendor evaluations, and provide them with the necessary portal access.

#### Periodically review the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal
Establish a process involving relevant stakeholders to conduct regular reviews of CORE content and implement a method for collecting and addressing clarification questions following material review.

```markdown
# Encryption
## Data in transit

### Customer responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform provides customers with encryption in transit via HTTPS for user access and API access to the instance. The platform also supports several protocols for integration with customer or third-party systems, including HTTPS, LDAPS, FTPS, and SCP. Customers should configure data in transit encryption methods in accordance with their security policies and use cases.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform supports default encryption in transit for sessions inbound to the instance using a minimum of TLS 1.2. All attempted access to a ServiceNow instance over HTTP is redirected to HTTPS.

ServiceNow instance email infrastructure supports opportunistic TLS for sending or receiving email.

---

### Best practices

#### Enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for browser connections
Customer admins should configure their web browsers to use only TLS 1.2, or higher when connecting to their ServiceNow instance.

## Use the Machine Identity Console
Use the [Machine Identity Console](#) to gain comprehensive visibility into the security posture of your inbound integrations, such as those used for service accounts, across the ServiceNow AI Platform.

## Review guidance around password spray attacks
Review the guidance in the [Password Spray Attack Mitigating Strategies (KB0726312)](#) (link requires a ServiceNow Support account) and work your security team to apply any relevant recommendations.

As of the Yokohama release, MFA is enabled by default for local logins, using built-in authentication. It is important to understand default MFA for local logins, high-privilege accounts, and sensitive roles. Teams should ensure that this default MFA setting is communicated to all relevant stakeholders. If a ServiceNow instance is not yet upgraded, enabling MFA for all admin users is recommended.

```markdown
# Identity and access management
## Authentication

### Customer responsibility
In the context of the Security [Shared Responsibility Model](#), customers have the responsibility of configuring their instance using supported authentication methods. This configuration process may include setting up multi-provider single sign-on (SSO) with security assertion markup language (SAML) or OpenID connect (OIDC), enabling smartcard authentication such as personal identity verification (PIV) or common access card (CAC) for environments requiring high security, utilizing OAuth, and enforcing multi-factor authentication (MFA).

## Adopt a proactive patch management process
Establish and follow a routine schedule to promptly install security patches and platform updates in both production and sub-production environments. Treat production and sub-production systems with equal diligence, ensuring that all environments are updated.

## Ensure instances remain on a supported family release
ServiceNow releases two major version updates per year and only supports the current version (N) and one prior release (N-1).

Instances operating on older family releases are categorized as “End-of-Life” (EOL) and do not receive new updates or patches. Organizations should establish and maintain a formal process to proactively track their ServiceNow instance’s family release version, ensuring timely upgrades before the platform reaches EOL status.

---

# Additional information

- [Commercial cloud vulnerability management SOP](Requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE here.)

### Ensure each user has a unique user account
Ensure that every user is assigned a unique user account within the system. This approach strengthens accountability, enables precise access management, and supports auditing of user activities.

### Machine Identity Console
A machine identity refers to a service account used for inbound API integrations. The Machine Identity Console provides visibility into these identities by listing all accounts with Web Service Access Enabled set to true and/or those that have accessed an API.

These identities are critical for automation, integration, and secure communication, but they’re often invisible and unmanaged. To maintain security and accountability, ensure that individual user accounts are separate from service accounts used for supporting unattended or automation processes.

#### Test changes in non-production first  
Before applying any configuration changes to a production environment, it is essential to test them in a non-production instance. This practice helps identify potential issues, ensures compatibility with existing workflows, and reduces the risk of service disruptions.

#### Understand and follow the ServiceNow Patching Program  
As the instance administrator, it is important to understand and follow the ServiceNow Patching Program. This program updates customer instances to required patch versions periodically throughout the year.

Through these updates, instances receive current security, performance, and functional fixes. Patching addresses known security vulnerabilities and forms a standard part of any patch management process.

---

November 2025 | Release: Zurich  
```

Customers should ensure that the [protected tables plugin](#) is enabled on their ServiceNow instance and that appropriate protection levels are configured. When the property `com.glide.security.protected_table.enabled` is set to true, the platform applies controls designed to prevent privileged users from tampering with critical log tables. This capability is essential for maintaining the integrity of audit data and reducing the risk of unauthorized changes.  

To implement protected tables effectively, security teams should review and define the correct protection levels and actions that align with their company policies. It is equally important to incorporate alerts into monitoring procedures so that any attempt to modify protected tables is detected promptly.  

By combining these measures, organizations can strengthen compliance, preserve operational transparency, and ensure that sensitive log data remains secure throughout its lifecycle.

---

---

## Best practices

### Choose an encryption method for data at rest in an instance*
The customer’s security team should work with stakeholders to thoroughly assess the regulatory and organizational requirements for data stored in their ServiceNow instance(s) to determine if data at rest needs to be encrypted.

Based on this assessment, customers should select the most appropriate encryption method offered by ServiceNow. When implementing the chosen encryption method, ensure encryption settings and key management are configured in accordance with internal policies and compliance standards to safeguard sensitive information throughout its lifecycle.

### Customers seeking included functionality
**Field Encryption Starter**:  
Data stored within a ServiceNow instance can be protected with Field Encryption Starter, which allows customers to encrypt specific fields within the instance using AES128 or AES256 encryption.

#### Manage IP address access control
Limit which IP addresses are allowed or denied access to the ServiceNow instance. If a VPN or another method is used to route traffic through a known set of IP addresses, access to the instance should only be allowed for that range of addresses.

**Note:** IP address access control does not limit access for ServiceNow support personnel. Customers can enable the [SNC access control plugin](#) to restrict instance access to specific personnel, or restrict access without their express permission. Enabling this plugin may affect the ability of ServiceNow support to help a customer if they are locked out of their instance.

#### Consider API authentication
API access can use either standard user identities (interactive) or machine identities (non-interactive). Evaluate your authentication from both perspectives.

## Understand how to review logs for investigations
One of the most important components of incident response is ServiceNow instance logs. These [system logs](https://support.servicenow.com), will be able to provide customers’ security teams with the necessary telemetry for their incident response investigations. Logs can be reviewed using a variety of methods, such as the [log file browser](https://support.servicenow.com), Table APIs, and directly in the platform.

## Conduct postmortem activities following a security incident
Following a security incident, it is important to perform a postmortem review of the investigations to determine possible improvements that can be made for future incident response activities. This can include identifying possible communication issues, gaps within the environment’s security posture, and ensuring all involved parties understand the root cause of the issue and how to avoid similar situations moving forward.

# MID Server security

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for ensuring the security of the MID Server by maintaining strict physical controls, deploying and hardening the server and operating system in accordance with their internal IT policies, and restricting network access to only essential services and infrastructure. They are also responsible for operating the MID Server and managing account credentials. Additionally, customers must monitor firewall and proxy configurations to allow only the necessary connections.

---

## Best practices

### Secure physical access to the MID Server
Place the MID Server in a physically secure location, such as a locked data center or server room, with access restricted to authorized personnel. Follow your organization’s access audit requirements to detect and prevent unauthorized entry.

*Note:* Negotiated ciphers are subject to customer browser versions and may be influenced by customer Internet proxy infrastructure. Customers can specify cipher suites in their own browsers or proxies, as well as select the ciphers to be used on their instance.

#### Configure other protocols for encryption in transit
Admins can also configure other traffic protocols, such as LDAP, SMTP, and SFTP, to use TLS 1.2.

#### Encrypt email via S/MIME
ServiceNow implementations can support [S/MIME “end-to-end” email encryption](https://www.servicenow.com).
```

```markdown
# Best practices continued

## Enhanced protective controls

### Implement Data Privacy for Now Assist
Engage stakeholders to assess the need and value of enabling [Data Privacy for Now Assist](#). This solution integrates with the [Generative AI Controller](#) and uses real-time anonymization with configurable data patterns to protect sensitive information before prompts are submitted to the LLM.

### Enable Now Assist Guardian for enhanced protection
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine whether Now Assist Guardian is needed to safeguard users and data. This feature monitors LLM requests and responses to detect offensive or harmful content, prompt injection attempts, and filtered topics. Offensive content and injection attempts can be logged or blocked based on your configuration. If a filter is triggered, users are redirected to the Sensitivity Detection: Fallback topic in Virtual Agent.

For detailed implementation guidance, refer to the [Now Assist Guardian](#) documentation.

### Best practices

#### Understand your organization’s incident response escalation channels
One of the most important variables during a security incident is the time between the incident being reported and when your security team is alerted. To minimize this time as much as possible, ensure that you understand the appropriate contacts within your organization that need to be alerted when an incident is reported. This could be an email address, a catalog item within your internal resources, or a post to a messaging channel. By understanding the initial steps to be taken, customers will be able to quickly respond to an incident, whether it is reported by a company resource or by [ServiceNow Support](#) cases or COMM records.

### Ensure each user has a unique user account
Ensure that every user is assigned a unique user account within the system. This approach strengthens accountability, enables precise access management, and supports auditing of user activities.

### Machine Identity Console
A machine identity refers to a service account used for inbound API integrations. The Machine Identity Console provides visibility into these identities by listing all accounts with Web Service Access Enabled set to true and/or those that have accessed an API.

These identities are critical for automation, integration, and secure communication, but they’re often invisible and unmanaged. To maintain security and accountability, ensure that individual user accounts are separate from service accounts used for supporting unattended or automation processes.

The key differences include accountability (individual vs system), licensing, authentication, and lifecycle management. Both require strict least privilege, but non-interactive accounts need extra controls like credential rotation, monitoring for unusual API activity, and clear ownership documentation to prevent unauthorized system access.

For integration accounts, enable the web services access flag to prevent those accounts from using interactive sessions.

### Define roles clearly
Identify each job function that will interact with the ServiceNow AI Platform and assign specific user roles with clear names and descriptions. Update roles as business needs evolve and communicate privileges to users. Adopt the concept of least-privileged access. This ensures effective access control and simplifies auditing.

## Evaluate and configure AI model options on the ServiceNow AI Platform
Some ServiceNow products rely on third-party Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) services, such as Azure OpenAI. Collaborate with your stakeholders to determine whether your organization will use these cloud-based models. If they do not meet your security or compliance requirements, configure ServiceNow to fully opt out of options like Microsoft Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, or Anthropic Claude on Amazon Web Services (AWS).

*Note:* Certain skills may restrict model provider selection, based on functional or technical limitations. These exceptions are described in [Model Provider Support Matrix for Now Assist Skills and AI Agents (KB2222333)](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=kb2222333), which outlines supported skills and agents for both the Now LLM and third-party OEM LLMs.

```markdown
# ServiceNow responsibility continued

## Backup restoration
If a customer deletes data inadvertently, or if a customer's data integration or automation gets misconfigured or malfunctions, this could render data unusable or inaccessible. In these scenarios, AHA architecture would not be able to recover the deleted data or data loss due to misconfiguration, because with AHA database replication occurs to both instances in the pair at near real-time. Restoring from **backup** is the only option for recovery.

ServiceNow can restore customer data upon request. For more information, see the [ServiceNow Backup and Restoration SOP](#) (link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#)).

## Media disposal and destruction
Media disposal and destruction refers to the disposal of hard drives in ServiceNow colocation facilities. ServiceNow follows NIST 800-88 guidelines for destroying hard drives and rendering the media infeasible for future use.

---

Built-in security metrics in the Security Center provide data on potential threats and trends, allowing users to observe key indicators and set up alerts. These metrics and dashboards are primarily intended for raising awareness rather than continuous monitoring. Organizations with more advanced needs can integrate a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) solution for real-time tracking and automated response. #### Configure and enforce strong password policies
It is important for customers to set password policies for their Identity Provider (IdP) and within their ServiceNow instance(s). This includes specifying requirements like minimum password length, complexity, expiration, uniqueness, and lockout conditions for native accounts. Also, be sure configurations meet your organizational standards.

#### Enable account lockout to prevent brute force attacks
As a critical security best practice, customers should enable account lockouts both on their IdP and for all local accounts within the ServiceNow instance. This measure is essential to defend against brute force authentication attacks by automatically locking accounts after a set number of failed login attempts.

# Request that the support case be marked as a security case
If a case being submitted involves confirmed compromise of customer information, customers are able to request the case be flagged as a security case, which limits the case visibility as needed. Ensure that security cases are intentionally designated as such. Customer visibility into a security case is limited to the submitter and any accounts designated on the case’s watchlist.

## Educate your security team on how to raise a case with ServiceNow Support
Ensure that your security team, or at a minimum, the designated security contact in [Security Contacts on ServiceNow Support](https://support.servicenow.com), has documentation on how to create a support case via [support.servicenow.com](https://support.servicenow.com) in the event they need to report an incident and cannot contact a member of the platform team.

## Security_Admin role
[High Security Settings](https://www.servicenow.com) and the [High Security plugin](https://www.servicenow.com) are activated by default on new ServiceNow instances and they can provide an elevated privilege role called `security_admin` role. This role allows users to create and change access controls and change High Security Settings. In the base system, only the default System Administrator (admin) user has the `security_admin` role. The customer admin should work with stakeholders, such as the company’s security team, to determine if an elevated role assignment is required. The `security_admin` role should be assigned to a limited number of users and groups.

## Best practice prioritization
Customers should evaluate each best practice in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to determine applicability and evaluate potential risks. Therefore, they must work closely with security and compliance teams when identifying the best practices to address.

#### Manage IP address access control
Limit which IP addresses are allowed or denied access to the ServiceNow instance. If a VPN or another method is used to route traffic through a known set of IP addresses, access to the instance should only be allowed for that range of addresses.

**Note:** IP address access control does not limit access for ServiceNow support personnel. Customers can enable the [SNC access control plugin](#) to restrict instance access to specific personnel, or restrict access without their express permission. Enabling this plugin may affect the ability of ServiceNow support to help a customer if they are locked out of their instance.

#### Consider API authentication
API access can use either standard user identities (interactive) or machine identities (non-interactive). Evaluate your authentication from both perspectives.

```markdown
# Best practices continued

## Know the difference between software updates and upgrades
Understanding the difference between a software update and an upgrade is essential for maintaining both security and support in your ServiceNow environment.

- **Software updates:** Patches and platform fixes delivered throughout the year via the ServiceNow Patching Program. These address known vulnerabilities and improve performance without changing the platform version.
- **Upgrades:** Moving to a newer major platform version, typically released twice a year, which includes enhanced features, architectural improvements, and broader functionality.

Both are critical but serve different purposes in keeping your instance secure, stable, and supported.

# MID Server security

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for ensuring the security of the MID Server by maintaining strict physical controls, deploying and hardening the server and operating system in accordance with their internal IT policies, and restricting network access to only essential services and infrastructure. They are also responsible for operating the MID Server and managing account credentials. Additionally, customers must monitor firewall and proxy configurations to allow only the necessary connections.

---

## Best practices

### Secure physical access to the MID Server
Place the MID Server in a physically secure location, such as a locked data center or server room, with access restricted to authorized personnel. Follow your organization’s access audit requirements to detect and prevent unauthorized entry.

### Ensure each user has a unique user account
Ensure that every user is assigned a unique user account within the system. This approach strengthens accountability, enables precise access management, and supports auditing of user activities.

### Machine Identity Console
A machine identity refers to a service account used for inbound API integrations. The Machine Identity Console provides visibility into these identities by listing all accounts with Web Service Access Enabled set to true and/or those that have accessed an API.

These identities are critical for automation, integration, and secure communication, but they’re often invisible and unmanaged. To maintain security and accountability, ensure that individual user accounts are separate from service accounts used for supporting unattended or automation processes.

# Authorization

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for defining user roles based on job functions and assigning appropriate permissions using role-based access control (RBAC) and access control lists (ACLs). It is recommended to configure ACLs to enforce the principle of least privilege and use non-production instances to test changes before deployment.

---

## Best practices

### Distinguish between interactive vs non-interactive user accounts
**Interactive user accounts** should use MFA and role-based access controls, ensuring least privilege and tying actions to individuals for accountability.

**Non-interactive accounts**, intended for integrations and automation, should authenticate via API keys or OAuth tokens, have roles restricted to their purpose, utilize IP restrictions when possible, and link actions to the system or team.

### Ensure each user has a unique user account
Ensure that every user is assigned a unique user account within the system. This approach strengthens accountability, enables precise access management, and supports auditing of user activities.

### Machine Identity Console
A machine identity refers to a service account used for inbound API integrations. The Machine Identity Console provides visibility into these identities by listing all accounts with Web Service Access Enabled set to true and/or those that have accessed an API.

These identities are critical for automation, integration, and secure communication, but they’re often invisible and unmanaged. To maintain security and accountability, ensure that individual user accounts are separate from service accounts used for supporting unattended or automation processes.

# Data management and privacy compliance
## Data controller and data processor

### Customer responsibility
As the data controller, the customer is responsible for determining how data is collected, stored, used, shared, archived, destroyed, and for maintaining the accuracy and confidentiality of that data. The customer is also responsible for meeting their requirements as a data controller under the applicable data protection laws.

Additionally, customers are responsible for risks associated with their AI investments. ServiceNow has a premium offering, called AI Control Tower, that can give customers visibility into their AI footprint by managing their AI asset inventory, configuration, state of AI cases, and approval flows.

For more detail on AI best practices refer to [AI security in the PROTECT section](#).

---

It is recommended that customers limit the use of personal identities for executing unattended automations or integrations. By implementing ServiceNow access policy restrictions to clearly separate these data flows, organizations can better define and uphold policies aligned with their identity architecture.

### Use security attributes when possible
Customers should utilize applicable security attributes when possible. Security attributes offer an alternative method for access control via role definitions.

### Use security data filters when possible
Security data filters enable access restriction to records based on a user’s role, or other security attribute-related assertions. Security data filters are applied before a query is executed and ensure only authorized users can view records regardless of how data is accessed. Customers should explicitly enable security data filters for user-facing queries that are not using GlideRecordSecure.

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow, as the data processor, supports customer incident response by querying backend logs upon request, subject to an eight-week retention limit. While customers are responsible for interpreting logs, [ServiceNow Support](#) can help review samples to clarify log types. However, it is essential to note that ServiceNow Support does not have the resources to analyze every event.

ServiceNow Support and security teams assist in identifying possible causes of incidents and offer preventive guidance, though recommendations may be limited by platform capabilities.

At an enterprise level, security teams at ServiceNow have implemented detection rules that initiate internal incident response processes. Detections related to customer instances are normally reported through a support case.

### Best practices

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
As the data processor, ServiceNow supports the data controllers by providing features to enable access and control of data processing activities and obligations.

ServiceNow has a dedicated Cloud Assurance team responsible for several governance and compliance efforts across the organization, including managing the ServiceNow compliance program. ServiceNow is reviewed on an annual basis by independent third-party auditors. ServiceNow will establish and maintain sufficient controls to meet certification and attestation for the objectives stated in ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701, 9001, 22301, 42001 (new AI/IT), and SSAE 18 SOC 2 Type 2 (or equivalent standards) for the security program.

---

### Best practices

#### Clarify stakeholder data responsibilities
Set up a process to regularly involve stakeholders in defining data responsibilities, making sure that controls meet internal policies and goals and are working as intended.

# Secure coding

Customers are responsible for any custom code they develop on the ServiceNow AI Platform. All custom development should follow secure coding best practices to minimize security risks.

## ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow follows a “build security in” strategy to identify and reduce risk throughout the Software Development Lifecycle. This approach includes security education, best practices, iterative security design, and continuous security analysis, enabling product teams to deliver robust and secure software.

## Best practices

**Customer responsibility**

**Best practices**  

### Create a process to update security contacts regularly  
Ensure the security contact record within ServiceNow Support is always kept up to date, with details of at least two appropriate information security personnel. Set a reminder to review the security contact details at least quarterly to ensure they are current and accurate.  

- Security contacts should be authorized to act on the information they receive, because it may be critically important to the organization.

Regularly review import logs to track data import activity, including source, status, and timing, to ensure data integrity and detect any anomalies.

Use API Analytics to monitor inbound API usage and users. Customers can track and analyze inbound REST and SOAP activity with API Analytics. These analytics help customers understand which APIs are being used, by whom, and to what degree.

#### Understand your organization’s incident response escalation channels
One of the most important variables during a security incident is the time between the incident being reported and when your security team is alerted. To minimize this time as much as possible, ensure that you understand the appropriate contacts within your organization that need to be alerted when an incident is reported. This could be an email address, a catalog item within your internal resources, or a post to a messaging channel. By understanding the initial steps to be taken, customers will be able to quickly respond to an incident, whether it is reported by a company resource or by [ServiceNow Support](#) cases or COMM records.

# ServiceNow responsibility continued

## Backup restoration
If a customer deletes data inadvertently, or if a customer's data integration or automation gets misconfigured or malfunctions, this could render data unusable or inaccessible. In these scenarios, AHA architecture would not be able to recover the deleted data or data loss due to misconfiguration, because with AHA database replication occurs to both instances in the pair at near real-time. Restoring from **backup** is the only option for recovery.

ServiceNow can restore customer data upon request. For more information, see the [ServiceNow Backup and Restoration SOP](#) (link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#)).

## Media disposal and destruction
Media disposal and destruction refers to the disposal of hard drives in ServiceNow colocation facilities. ServiceNow follows NIST 800-88 guidelines for destroying hard drives and rendering the media infeasible for future use.

# Key concepts and reference material

## Intended audience
This guide is specifically designed for instance administrators to collaborate closely with security and compliance professionals. Engaging both parties is essential to effectively address the evolving landscape of digital threats, demonstrate due diligence, and sustain a robust security posture across the ServiceNow environment.

## Identify stakeholders
At the outset of a best practice review, instance administrators are advised to identify the primary security and compliance stakeholders within their organization. Their expertise and insights will help tailor the best practices to the organization’s specific risk profile and compliance requirements.

Engaging these partners early in the process not only streamlines decision making but also strengthens the organization’s overall security posture throughout the ServiceNow environment.

ServiceNow provides the current versions of these addenda on [Legal: Customer Agreements and Terms](https://www.servicenow.com) for general understanding; however, to understand the specific details, administrators are advised to reach out to their own compliance or legal support team.  

---

### Best practices  

#### Review and understand the DSA and DPA terms and conditions  
Consult with your compliance and legal teams to ensure they have read and understand the ServiceNow DSA and/or DPA.  

#### Where applicable, review the ServiceNow third party hosted product addendum  
Work with compliance and legal teams to address any questions regarding the use of ServiceNow subscription products that use data hosting provided by third-party sub-processors (third party hosted products).  

---

```markdown
# Secure coding

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for any custom code they develop on the ServiceNow AI Platform. All custom development should follow secure coding best practices to minimize security risks.

## ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow follows a “build security in” strategy to identify and reduce risk throughout the Software Development Lifecycle. This approach includes security education, best practices, iterative security design, and continuous security analysis, enabling product teams to deliver robust and secure software.

## Best practices

### Review ServiceNow Software Development Lifecycle SOP
Regularly review the ServiceNow [Software Development Lifecycle SOP](https://www.servicenow.com/) with stakeholders, such as security and compliance teams, to ensure everyone understands the process and can address any questions (link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](https://www.servicenow.com/)).

## Understand the difference between Allow-If and Deny-Unless ACLs
Allow-If allows access upon successful evaluation and is the default ACL. Deny-Unless denies access unless there is a successful evaluation. Deny-Unless ACLs will take priority against Allow-If ACLs in ACL Evaluation as it will be evaluated first. The Deny-Unless ACL defines the users that will NOT be denied. Said another way, the user will be denied access unless the role, condition, and script requirements are met.

## Verify Security Jump Start—ACL Rules Plugin is enabled
All new ServiceNow instances have the [Security Jump Start—ACL Rules plugin](#) installed to provide a base level of access security for key system tables. Use this plugin to establish foundational ACL protections for sensitive system data.

The assessment typically spans several months and follows an iterative process where findings are remediated by ServiceNow security and development teams. Results of these penetration tests are available to customers and prospects under NDA via the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal.

## Best practices

### Create a process to examine ServiceNow penetration test reports periodically
Create a process to ensure stakeholders, such as your security team, review the most recent published [ServiceNow penetration test reports](#) on the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#).

## Data processing in production
When using generative AI services, prompts and responses are processed in memory only—inputs and outputs are not stored or cached by the inference infrastructure. For details on how data is transmitted, processed, and protected during runtime, refer to the [Data Processing for Advanced AI & Data Products FAQ (KB1584492)](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=kb1584492).

Evaluate how AI data is securely processed and select either ServiceNow-hosted or third-party LLMs in alignment with your organization’s data residency and governance policies.

*Note:* Third-party LLMs may use global infrastructure to dynamically route traffic to the best available data center for each request. This means the regional processing location may differ from the data center region specified on a customer’s order form.

```markdown
# Identity and access management
## Authentication

### Customer responsibility
In the context of the Security [Shared Responsibility Model](#), customers have the responsibility of configuring their instance using supported authentication methods. This configuration process may include setting up multi-provider single sign-on (SSO) with security assertion markup language (SAML) or OpenID connect (OIDC), enabling smartcard authentication such as personal identity verification (PIV) or common access card (CAC) for environments requiring high security, utilizing OAuth, and enforcing multi-factor authentication (MFA).

```markdown
# Email security

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for configuring email security features within the ServiceNow AI Platform to align with their organization’s security posture and business requirements. The platform allows instances to generate and receive emails for common workflows such as task assignments, change management approvals, and status notifications. Users can also update or respond to requests by replying to these emails. While ServiceNow provides multiple out-of-the-box features to support email security, it is the customer’s responsibility to enable and manage these features appropriately to protect their instance and data.

---

## Best practices

### Enable email filters and malware protection
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine if the organization needs to use the ServiceNow AI Platform email filter features to manage inbound messages and restrict accepted sender domains.

#### Manage IP address access control
Limit which IP addresses are allowed or denied access to the ServiceNow instance. If a VPN or another method is used to route traffic through a known set of IP addresses, access to the instance should only be allowed for that range of addresses.

**Note:** IP address access control does not limit access for ServiceNow support personnel. Customers can enable the [SNC access control plugin](#) to restrict instance access to specific personnel, or restrict access without their express permission. Enabling this plugin may affect the ability of ServiceNow support to help a customer if they are locked out of their instance.

#### Consider API authentication
API access can use either standard user identities (interactive) or machine identities (non-interactive). Evaluate your authentication from both perspectives.

#### Align with change management
Changes to ServiceNow instances should follow the organization’s change management process. Document each activity with an official record and obtain approvals before proceeding to ensure tracking, authorization, and compliance.

#### Plan for acceptable use
Customers should work with all stakeholders to define appropriate usage guidelines for ServiceNow. This guidance should be published in the organizational standards, when appropriate. Manage instance activity in accordance with company guidelines throughout each instance’s lifecycle.

#### Retire unused instances
Decommission ServiceNow instances that are no longer needed, following the organization’s documented retirement process that includes backing up critical data, removing all integrations and credentials, and updating the centralized inventory to reflect changes.

### Additional information
- [Requesting instance retire via service catalog on ServiceNow Support](#) (requires a ServiceNow Support account)

---

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow operates a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system to review and correlate logs from multiple network and infrastructure sources. A Scheduled Security Operations Checklist is in place, which includes daily reviews of:
- Linux and Windows systems  
- Network devices  
- Intrusion Detection System (IDS) alerts  
- Behavioral and identified issue logs  

High-risk issues, such as intrusion detection events, trigger real-time alerts that are immediately sent to the Security Incident Response Team for review. Network and infrastructure log events are retained for a minimum of 90 days.

---

### Best practices

### Key ownership and control
Customers need to determine which type of encryption key they will use on the ServiceNow AI Platform: a ServiceNow-managed key (SMK) or bring your own key (BYOK).

### Encryption key lifecycle management
- **Generation**: When using BYOK, keys should be generated in accordance with the company’s internal security policy and follow the [ServiceNow key preparation guidance](https://example.com).
- **Rotation**: Customers should regularly rotate keys to minimize exposure. ServiceNow supports scheduled rotation for SMK and provides notification reminders for BYOK.
- **Storage**: BYOK’s should be stored in a secure, protected environment that performs regular backups to ensure that the keys remain available and recoverable, if needed.

---

## Best practices

# IDENTIFY

## Instance management

### Customer responsibility
Customers must oversee all the organization’s production and sub-production ServiceNow instances, ensuring each one’s purpose, owner, and data classification are known.

### Best practices

#### Maintain a centralized inventory of instances
Maintain a centralized, up-to-date inventory of all ServiceNow instances (see the [ServiceNow Support Instances Dashboard](#)). Clearly identify each instance by name and URL, environment type (such as Production, Development, Test, or Sandbox), business purpose, designated business and technical owners, and data classification.

#### Regularly review all instances
Conduct regular reviews of all production and sub-production ServiceNow instances to verify each instance’s ownership, purpose, and ongoing alignment with business needs. Document each review and its findings and formalize the follow-up process to support continuous oversight.

```markdown
# Data management and privacy compliance
## Data controller and data processor

### Customer responsibility
As the data controller, the customer is responsible for determining how data is collected, stored, used, shared, archived, destroyed, and for maintaining the accuracy and confidentiality of that data. The customer is also responsible for meeting their requirements as a data controller under the applicable data protection laws.

Additionally, customers are responsible for risks associated with their AI investments. ServiceNow has a premium offering, called AI Control Tower, that can give customers visibility into their AI footprint by managing their AI asset inventory, configuration, state of AI cases, and approval flows.

For more detail on AI best practices refer to [AI security in the PROTECT section](#).

---

```markdown
# Mobile application security

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for implementing and maintaining security measures that protect their ServiceNow mobile environment. This includes enforcing strong authentication methods such as MFA, managing user privileges, and configuring mobile security settings to align with the organizational policies and standards.

---

## Best practices

### Configure mobile application security controls
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine the configuration of built-in mobile security controls. This process should include reviewing the following controls to ensure alignment with organizational policies and standards: clipboard restrictions, disabling screenshots, preventing attachments, requiring an in-app PIN, and enabling background blur.

## Understand the difference between Allow-If and Deny-Unless ACLs
Allow-If allows access upon successful evaluation and is the default ACL. Deny-Unless denies access unless there is a successful evaluation. Deny-Unless ACLs will take priority against Allow-If ACLs in ACL Evaluation as it will be evaluated first. The Deny-Unless ACL defines the users that will NOT be denied. Said another way, the user will be denied access unless the role, condition, and script requirements are met.

## Verify Security Jump Start—ACL Rules Plugin is enabled
All new ServiceNow instances have the [Security Jump Start—ACL Rules plugin](#) installed to provide a base level of access security for key system tables. Use this plugin to establish foundational ACL protections for sensitive system data.

# Email security

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for configuring email security features within the ServiceNow AI Platform to align with their organization’s security posture and business requirements. The platform allows instances to generate and receive emails for common workflows such as task assignments, change management approvals, and status notifications. Users can also update or respond to requests by replying to these emails. While ServiceNow provides multiple out-of-the-box features to support email security, it is the customer’s responsibility to enable and manage these features appropriately to protect their instance and data.

---

## Best practices

### Enable email filters and malware protection
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine if the organization needs to use the ServiceNow AI Platform email filter features to manage inbound messages and restrict accepted sender domains.

### Monitor email and malware metrics
Collaborate with stakeholders to establish effective monitoring of email and anti-malware activity. Configure alerts to proactively identify abnormal email activity or potential malware threats and have documented mitigation measures. There are metrics available in the ServiceNow Security Center (SSC) to review.

### Encrypt email with TLS and S/MIME
ServiceNow mail infrastructure is designed to use opportunistic TLS to encrypt email in transit. Ensure the organization’s sending and receiving email infrastructure supports this setting.

ServiceNow also supports the Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) standard. S/MIME is an end-to-end encryption protocol for sending digitally signed and encrypted emails, ensuring data confidentiality, authenticity, and integrity. Collaborate with stakeholders to determine if this feature should be configured.

# Secure coding

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for any custom code they develop on the ServiceNow AI Platform. All custom development should follow secure coding best practices to minimize security risks.

## ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow follows a “build security in” strategy to identify and reduce risk throughout the Software Development Lifecycle. This approach includes security education, best practices, iterative security design, and continuous security analysis, enabling product teams to deliver robust and secure software.

## Best practices

### Review ServiceNow Software Development Lifecycle SOP
Regularly review the ServiceNow [Software Development Lifecycle SOP](https://www.servicenow.com/) with stakeholders, such as security and compliance teams, to ensure everyone understands the process and can address any questions (link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](https://www.servicenow.com/)).

The key differences include accountability (individual vs system), licensing, authentication, and lifecycle management. Both require strict least privilege, but non-interactive accounts need extra controls like credential rotation, monitoring for unusual API activity, and clear ownership documentation to prevent unauthorized system access.

For integration accounts, enable the web services access flag to prevent those accounts from using interactive sessions.

### Define roles clearly
Identify each job function that will interact with the ServiceNow AI Platform and assign specific user roles with clear names and descriptions. Update roles as business needs evolve and communicate privileges to users. Adopt the concept of least-privileged access. This ensures effective access control and simplifies auditing.

# RECOVER

## Business continuity and disaster recovery

### Customer responsibility
While ServiceNow manages infrastructure-level disaster recovery and system failover, customers should create and maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans tailored to their processes and risk tolerance for their ServiceNow instance. This plan should include developing internal communication and response strategies.

By proactively addressing these responsibilities, customers help ensure their organization is prepared to respond quickly and effectively in the event of an unexpected disruption.

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow operates a disaster recovery program for customer instances called the [Information System Contingency Plan (ISCP)](https://www.servicenow.com/). (Link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](https://www.servicenow.com/).)

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow operates a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system to review and correlate logs from multiple network and infrastructure sources. A Scheduled Security Operations Checklist is in place, which includes daily reviews of:
- Linux and Windows systems  
- Network devices  
- Intrusion Detection System (IDS) alerts  
- Behavioral and identified issue logs  

High-risk issues, such as intrusion detection events, trigger real-time alerts that are immediately sent to the Security Incident Response Team for review. Network and infrastructure log events are retained for a minimum of 90 days.

---

### Best practices

#### Test changes in non-production first  
Before applying any configuration changes to a production environment, it is essential to test them in a non-production instance. This practice helps identify potential issues, ensures compatibility with existing workflows, and reduces the risk of service disruptions.

#### Understand and follow the ServiceNow Patching Program  
As the instance administrator, it is important to understand and follow the ServiceNow Patching Program. This program updates customer instances to required patch versions periodically throughout the year.

Through these updates, instances receive current security, performance, and functional fixes. Patching addresses known security vulnerabilities and forms a standard part of any patch management process.

---

November 2025 | Release: Zurich  
```

Use the MFA Dashboard to gain MFA insights such as user enrollment, privileged admins who haven’t opted in to MFA, and compliance. To enhance instance security, the MFA dashboard will help customer admins confirm that all users have enabled MFA.

Allow-If allows access upon successful evaluation and is the default ACL. Deny-Unless denies access unless there is a successful evaluation. Deny-Unless ACLs will take priority against Allow-If ACLs in ACL Evaluation as it will be evaluated first. The Deny-Unless ACL defines the users that will NOT be denied. ## Evaluate and configure AI model options on the ServiceNow AI Platform
Some ServiceNow products rely on third-party Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) services, such as Azure OpenAI. Collaborate with your stakeholders to determine whether your organization will use these cloud-based models. If they do not meet your security or compliance requirements, configure ServiceNow to fully opt out of options like Microsoft Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, or Anthropic Claude on Amazon Web Services (AWS).

*Note:* Certain skills may restrict model provider selection, based on functional or technical limitations. These exceptions are described in [Model Provider Support Matrix for Now Assist Skills and AI Agents (KB2222333)](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=kb2222333), which outlines supported skills and agents for both the Now LLM and third-party OEM LLMs.

## Adopt a proactive patch management process
Establish and follow a routine schedule to promptly install security patches and platform updates in both production and sub-production environments. Treat production and sub-production systems with equal diligence, ensuring that all environments are updated.

## Ensure instances remain on a supported family release
ServiceNow releases two major version updates per year and only supports the current version (N) and one prior release (N-1).

Instances operating on older family releases are categorized as “End-of-Life” (EOL) and do not receive new updates or patches. Organizations should establish and maintain a formal process to proactively track their ServiceNow instance’s family release version, ensuring timely upgrades before the platform reaches EOL status.

# Encryption
## Data in transit

### Customer responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform provides customers with encryption in transit via HTTPS for user access and API access to the instance. The platform also supports several protocols for integration with customer or third-party systems, including HTTPS, LDAPS, FTPS, and SCP. Customers should configure data in transit encryption methods in accordance with their security policies and use cases.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform supports default encryption in transit for sessions inbound to the instance using a minimum of TLS 1.2. All attempted access to a ServiceNow instance over HTTP is redirected to HTTPS.

ServiceNow instance email infrastructure supports opportunistic TLS for sending or receiving email.

---

### Best practices

#### Enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for browser connections
Customer admins should configure their web browsers to use only TLS 1.2, or higher when connecting to their ServiceNow instance.

## ServiceNow responsibility

ServiceNow is committed to building and deploying AI responsibly. Our generative AI solutions are designed with human-centric principles, ensuring customers remain in control.

ServiceNow maintains documented AI governance policies and standard procedures that incorporate industry best practices, including AI data governance, dataset lifecycle management, AI development, and deployment. These policies are regularly updated to address emerging technologies, evolving industry standards, and new security threats.

The ServiceNow AI governance process aligns with the NIST Risk Management Framework for AI and complies with all applicable local laws and regulations. As regulations evolve, we continue to adopt, expand, and align with relevant compliance programs to ensure ongoing adherence.
